newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Huge South Pacific earthquake stirs tidal wave.
newsitem.headline: Huge South Pacific earthquake stirs tidal wave.

text.p: Australian seismologists on Tuesday said they had recorded a huge earthquake deep in the Pacific Ocean but the scattered island nations of the South Pacific reported little damage from a resulting tsunami.
The earthquake, recorded by University of Queensland scientists late on Monday, measured 7.9 on the Richter Scale and was centred near the Santa Cruz islands in the Solomon Islands.

University of Queensland seismologist Steve Jaume said the earthquake was the largest recorded anywhere in the world this year. "Earthquakes of this size only occur about once a year," Jaume said in a statement.

Vanuatu emergency services said there was no damage from the earthquake but that a number of homes in the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu had been damaged by a subsequent tidal wave measuring almost three metres (nine feet).
There were no reports of casualties.
